# Results

Let $\alpha > 0$ and $\beta \in \mathbb{R}$.

## Theorem 1

For any $n \geq 1$, we have

$$\int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} dx = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}$$

The matrix representation is

$$\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$$

## Proof

The proof follows from $f(x) = \frac{1}{x}$ and the fact that $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} x^k = \frac{1}{1-x}$ for $|x| < 1$.
